label: First token of the sequence, for a fixed subset of 18 tokens
explanation: Fires essentially only at step 0, and only when the first original token is one of b g i k m n o p s t u v w x z 0 1 2. Since h0 is fixed, the step-0 activation depends only on the token: each of these 18 tokens fires on 100% of its step-0 occurrences, and the other 12 (a c d e f h j l q r y 3) never fire. Magnitude is set by token identity: t is strongest (~0.67 of max), then i, o, p, m; v and b are barely above threshold. It does not fire at any later original step, at the delimiter, or during the copy phase, with one small exception (2.7% of mass): when L=3, at step 4 (the first copy step, where orig(0) is fed back in right after <DEL>) it fires again for the same tokens, and these give the largest activations (max, e.g. t). Adding (L==3)&(t==4) to the predicate raises dev F1 from 0.986 to 0.994.

issues: The main claim holds on the test split. The predicate has precision 1.000, recall 0.972 and mass recall 0.972, with 0 false positives. The 12 excluded tokens never fire at t==0 (precision 0 for (t==0)&~set). The unit never fires at t=1-3, t>=5 or at the delimiter.

One secondary claim is inaccurate. At L==3, t==4 the unit does not fire 'for the same tokens'. Tokens outside the set fire there 49% of the time (for example d in 'd l 0 <DEL> [d]'), and tokens in the set fire only 80% of the time. So the copy-step exception is only partly selective for tokens, not a clean repeat of the step-0 rule.

The only systematic miss class is L==3, t==4 (2.8% of activation mass). The explanation acknowledges it and the label leaves it out, which is a minor understatement. The step-4 activations are not clearly concentrated in the top quartile: the set-token version covers only 2.1% of the top quartile, so 'these are the largest activations' is overstated, apart from the single maximum.
